name: THE STORAGE YARD
rule: VAMILY rules 416 (the big interiors: the tile stays a house), 461 (more boards), 451(a) (its ceiling at 10%), 59 (every tile its cost and its effect), 428, 441.
facts: The map lays self-storage along the streets ('self-storage sprawl', engine/bohemia_overmap.js) and gives it a share of every works zone (LAND_USE industry: industrial 0.5, warehouse 0.35, storage 0.15).
The dead's own line for the kind (engine/bohemia_dead.js): 'people lived in the units. some never opened again'.

A self-storage yard is a climate-controlled building of units off long halls (roll-up doors, a freight lift, hand carts by the doors), drive-up rows outside, and, in Las Vegas, RV and boat parking under steel canopies. People living in storage units and in stored RVs is a real thing when rent runs out.
On house tiles a run of shut units is a wall that hides a man; a unit with its door up is a small room a man fights from; an RV, a boat on its trailer and a moving truck each hide a man.
how_to_mod: A layout is 15 strings of 20 characters; every character is in 'legend'; every tile kind a legend entry names has its row in 'tiles' (its cost and its effect). A piece names the finished piece it is drawn as ('like') until this folder has its own art file (storage_art.json: floor lists and a kit, the garage's format). slices/bohemia_big_inside.js lays it; slices/fight_ground/insides.json lists the insides.
districts_why: The yard is its buildings, its drive-up rows and its canopy: about two fights in five there are fought inside the unit halls or under the canopy, by the cell's own dice; the rest in the drive-up rows, on the works yard.
tiles_how: Rule 59: every kind of tile says what it costs to step on and what it does. 'row' is the fight's own ground row (flat 2 AP, rough 3, height +1 a level, obstacles none); 'open' is open floor (on AUTO nobody stays on it); 'good' is ground AUTO goes to; 'say' is the one line he reads when he taps it (draft, the fewest words); 'sight' says whether a blocker hides a man ('blocked', the obstacles row) or is seen past ('seen'). [bb] each kind is a Battle Brothers ground: flat, rough, an obstacle, and cover as its trees and walls give it.

wall.effect: The yard's block wall: no way through, no sight through.

floor.effect: The hall's sealed concrete, the canopy's asphalt: open ground, nothing to hide behind; on AUTO nobody stays on it.

units.effect: A run of units, the roll-up doors down and padlocked: nobody stands there, and nobody sees through it; cover beside it. People lived in the units; some never opened again. [bb] its wall.

openunit.effect: A unit with its door rolled up, a steel box a man stands in to shoot out of: cover. [bb] its palisade.

livedin.effect: A unit somebody lived in when the rent stopped: a mattress, a camp stove, a life in boxes to the ceiling: cover.
livedin.say: A unit somebody lived in: cover.

boxes.effect: Moving boxes stacked higher than a man, dragged out of a unit: cover.

carts.effect: The yard's hand carts and flatbeds, left by the doors: low cover.

spill.effect: A unit's insides tipped across the floor, picked through: slow going (3 AP), low cover. [bb] its brush.
spill.say: Somebody's stuff underfoot: slow going, low cover.

furniture.effect: Somebody's couch and dresser, pulled out into the hall: cover.

lift.effect: The freight lift's shaft, its gate chained: nobody stands there, and nobody sees through it. [bb] its wall.

rv.effect: An RV in its stall under the canopy, its tyres flat: nobody stands there, and nobody sees through it; cover beside it. [bb] its boulder.

boat.effect: A boat on its trailer, a lake away from any water: nobody stands there, and nobody sees through it; cover beside it. [bb] its boulder.

truck.effect: A rental moving truck, its box full of somebody's last move: nobody stands there, and nobody sees through it. [bb] its boulder.

car.effect: A car under its cover, kept for a better time: cover.

awning.effect: An RV's awning rolled out, a cooler, chairs, a tarp hung for a wall: somebody lives in this one: cover.
awning.say: Somebody's camp by an RV: cover.

gear.effect: Jerry cans and a generator chained to the stall: low cover.
gear.say: Cans and a generator: low cover.

tyres.effect: Trailer tyres stacked in the aisle: low cover.

fire.effect: A fire somebody keeps in a drum. It burns day and night: a man in its light is seen.
fire.say_lit: A fire: you stand in its light, and they see you.

doors.effect: The hall's doors and the canopy's gate, open onto the drive-up rows: open ground, and by day the light falls in: a man here is seen.
doors.say_lit: The doors: open ground, and the day is on you.

kit_how: Every piece is drawn AS a finished piece of another kit ('like') until COOK's own picture for it is in storage_art.json under the same name: then that picture is used and nothing here changes. 'kind' is what it does in the fight (COVER, LOW_COVER, WALL); 'blocks_move' means nobody stands on its tile.
start_why: NO HIGH GROUND: an RV's roof is a ladder nobody climbs under fire on house tiles; the hall is one floor here, the lift is chained.

ceiling.how: VAMILY rule 451(a): the hall's ceiling grid and the canopy's steel and panels, over the board at this alpha. 'src' is the picture COOK makes; 'have' true the day it is in the folder. Until then the fight draws 'kind' itself, a stand-in (the warehouse's roof).
